title: Homemade Pepperoni Pizza
subtitle: two chewy, golden homemade crusts with a quick tomato sauce, lots of mozzarella and crisp-edged pepperoni
imageAlt: A homemade pepperoni pizza with bubbling mozzarella, one slice pulled out, on a navy napkin
servingsNote: 2 large pizzas: dinner for one big eater + one hungry eater, plus 2 lunches

beforeYouStart.text: The dough needs 1 hour to rise. Heat the oven to its hottest for at least 20 minutes before baking.
Choose mild pepperoni; check the label.

items.name: olive oil
items.note: 1 for the dough, 1 for the bowl and pans

steps.title: Dough
steps.text: Whisk the flour, yeast, sugar and salt in a large bowl. Add the warm water and 1 tbsp of the oil, stir to a shaggy dough, then knead on the counter 5–6 minutes until smooth and springy.

steps.title: Rise
steps.text: Put it in a bowl rubbed with a little of the remaining oil, cover and let rise 1 hour, until doubled. After 30 minutes, heat the oven to 260°C (500°F), or as hot as it goes, with racks in the lower and upper thirds.

steps.title: Sauce
steps.text: Stir the tomato sauce, dried oregano, garlic powder and salt together.

steps.title: Shape
steps.text: Punch the dough down, divide in 2 and stretch each into a 30 cm round on 2 baking sheets brushed with the last of the oil. If it springs back, rest it 5 minutes and stretch again.

steps.title: Top
steps.text: Spread the sauce thinly to 1 cm from the edge, then cover with the mozzarella and pepperoni.

steps.title: Bake
steps.text: Bake 12–15 minutes, swapping the pans halfway, until the crust is deep golden underneath and the cheese bubbles and browns.

fixIt.fix: The water was too hot or the yeast old. Water should feel warm, not hot, on your wrist.
Use less sauce, and bake on the lowest rack for the last 3 minutes.
It needs to relax: cover and rest 10 minutes, then stretch with your knuckles, not a rolling pin.

saleTip: Mozzarella is often $4.99 for 320 g on sale at No Frills; buy two and freeze one.
swap: Store-bought pizza dough: about 900 g for two pizzas; let it sit out 30 minutes so it stretches easily.
leftovers: Reheat slices in a covered dry skillet for a crisp bottom.
doneness: Pepperoni is a cured, ready-to-eat meat; bake until the cheese bubbles and the crust bottom is browned. Reheat leftovers to 74°C (165°F).
source: Based on tested homemade pizza dough methods (King Arthur Baking, Canadian Living): an instant-yeast dough risen 1 hour, a quick no-cook sauce, baked on sheet pans at the oven's highest heat.
prepAhead: Make the dough up to 2 days ahead and keep it covered in the fridge; it gets more flavour. Bring it out 1 hour before shaping.
Freeze dough balls up to 3 months.
reheat: Slices in a covered dry skillet over medium 3–4 minutes, or the air fryer at 190°C for 3 minutes, until 74°C (165°F).

basic.note: Cheese pizza: sauce and mozzarella only.

fancy.note: Garlic-butter crust with Parmesan and a drizzle of honey over the pepperoni.

addSteps.title: Fancy finish
addSteps.text: Brush the hot crust edges with the butter mixed with the garlic powder, sprinkle the Parmesan over them and drizzle the honey over the top.

plating: Serve on a board, cut in 8.
Pull one slice out a little so the cheese stretches.

why.0-2: A little sugar helps the yeast get going and browns the crust.
why.1-0: A no-cook sauce stays bright; it cooks on the pizza.
why.2-0: Shredded low-moisture mozzarella melts and browns without making the pizza wet.

funFact: The word 'pepperoni' is an American take on the Italian 'peperoni', which in Italy means peppers, not sausage.
